rv.q: The success of Mr. Garcia’s play lies in the fact the audience will seriously consider how justice is played out in hearings like this every day.
Still, it holds your interest and, at an hour and 15 minutes (a bit longer than a TV episode), gives you something to talk about on the way to the subway.
Unfortunately, when it comes to The Witness Room , I doubt the jury will buy it.

Yet, whether or not one agrees with the show’s worldview, the production that is opening tonight at AMT Theater is ultimately unpersuasive as a pointed slice-of-life legal drama, because some missteps both undermine its verisimilitude and lessen its dramatic impact.
And what follows is a compelling peek into the lives and interactions of NYPD cops, their legal maneuverings in pretrial, and how slippery their moral code can get.

cn.t: Garcia's gritty cop drama about justice system corruption offers authentic legal detail and fierce performances, but critics find the execution uneven—praising its ambition while citing heavy-handed storytelling and familiar territory.
